name: MK-3984

lead: MK-3984 is a little-documented SARM candidate targeting muscle and bone, which muscle-building communities occasionally list as a lean-mass candidate.

As a SARM it is designed to act on androgen receptors in muscle and bone. The only dedicated study found is a 2026 doping-control study mapping its metabolism in zebrafish. No clinical trials or human data exist.

paras: There is no established routine; it appears mainly in discussions of lesser-known SARMs.
Human safety is unknown, and it is not approved for any use.

angle.text: MK-3984 is an obscure SARM that muscle-building communities occasionally list as a lean-mass candidate. It is designed to act on androgen receptors in muscle and bone. Published work is limited to a doping-control metabolite study in zebrafish, with no human data.

lead: MK-3984 is an experimental selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) targeting muscle and bone tissue.[1] Very little published information exists: it is mentioned in the SARM literature [2] and has been the subject of a 2026 doping-control study of its metabolism in zebrafish.[1]
No clinical trials or human data were found, and it is not approved for any use.

paras: No studies found. A review of SARMs for cancer-related muscle wasting discusses the drug class, and a laboratory study mapped the compound's metabolites in zebrafish, identifying 82 metabolites and 12 metabolic pathways, with reductive defluorination dominating phase I metabolism.[2][1]
The metabolite study was aimed at doping control, indicating interest in detecting the compound.[1] The sources reviewed do not document use of MK-3984 in looksmaxxing communities.
